question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Entertement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Entertement" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Entertainment", meaning an activity that provides amusement or enjoyment. (मनोरंजन)

◦ Example: The circus is a great source of entertainment for children.

• Spelling key: ENTER + TAIN + MENT — note the "tain" (from "entertain").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Conscious", "Celebrate" and "Outburst" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: entertain (verb), entertainer (noun), entertaining (adjective), entertainment (noun). Watch the "-tain-" in the middle (entertain → entertainment).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

jeopardy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. safety.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jeopardy" means danger of loss, harm or failure; risk. Its antonym is "safety", meaning the state of being protected from danger. (जोखिम/संकट का विलोम — सुरक्षा)

◦ Example: His life was in jeopardy, but the rescue team brought him to safety.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mighty" (powerful), Option 3 "strict" (severe) and Option 4 "silence" (quietness) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of jeopardy: danger, risk, peril, hazard, threat.

• Antonyms: safety, security, protection. "In jeopardy" = at risk / in danger.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Gracious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Rude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gracious" means kind, polite, courteous and pleasant. Its antonym is "rude", meaning impolite and bad-mannered. (शिष्ट/कृपालु का विलोम — असभ्य)

◦ Example: The host was gracious to all the guests, unlike his rude brother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Mythical" (imaginary/legendary), Option 3 "Keen" (eager) and Option 4 "Lonely" (solitary) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gracious: courteous, polite, kind, cordial, benevolent.

• Antonyms: rude, discourteous, impolite, ungracious.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The manager swiftly overtook him, __________ effortlessly past the skinny Englishman, with a practiced ease.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sliding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sliding" means moving smoothly and effortlessly along a surface. It fits "swiftly overtook ... effortlessly past ... with a practiced ease". (फिसलते हुए / सहजता से आगे बढ़ते हुए)

◦ Correct: The manager swiftly overtook him, sliding effortlessly past the skinny Englishman ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "kindling" (setting on fire / arousing), Option 2 "dawdling" (moving slowly / wasting time — the opposite of swift) and Option 4 "rendering" (giving/providing) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Dawdling" is a good trap here — it means moving slowly, which contradicts "swiftly overtook". "Sliding" correctly conveys smooth, effortless movement.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He is habituated to using words spoken with an unusual amount of venom when it comes to his in-laws.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. benevolence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "venom" means bitterness, spite or malice (extreme ill-will). Its antonym is "benevolence", meaning kindness and goodwill. (विद्वेष/कटुता का विलोम — परोपकार/सद्भावना)

◦ Example: His words were full of venom, showing no trace of benevolence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "satire" (mocking humour), Option 3 "ambiguousness" (vagueness) and Option 4 "irony" (saying the opposite of what is meant) are unrelated to the "malice" sense.

NOTE

• "Venom" literally means the poison of a snake; figuratively, it means spite/malice.

• Synonyms (figurative): malice, spite, bitterness. Antonyms: benevolence, kindness, goodwill.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The success and achievements of a school mostly __________ on its experience and resourcefulness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. depend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "depend" collocates with the preposition "on" and means to be determined by / rely on. The success of a school depends on its experience and resourcefulness. (निर्भर करना)

◦ Correct: The success and achievements of a school mostly depend on its experience and resourcefulness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "credit", 2 "achieve" and 3 "begin" do not collocate with "on" in this sense and do not fit the meaning.

NOTE

• "Depend on/upon" = to rely on / be determined by. The plural subject "success and achievements" takes the base verb "depend".

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling error in the following sentence.

The poet was able to compose the long poem in a tranquill atmosphere.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. tranquil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "tranquil", meaning calm, peaceful and quiet. (शांत / निश्चल)

◦ Example: The lake looked beautiful and tranquil at dawn.

• Spelling key: TRAN + QUIL — single "l" at the end (not double).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "trankwil", 3 "trancuel" and 4 "tranquel" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Related words: tranquil (adjective), tranquillity/tranquility (noun), tranquillise (verb). Synonyms: calm, serene, peaceful, placid, still.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

He will be / waiting for me when / I reaches his home.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I reaches his home.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pronoun "I" takes the base verb in the simple present, not the "-s" form. So "I reaches" is wrong; it should be "I reach".

◦ Correct: He will be waiting for me when I reach his home.

• In a clause referring to the future (introduced by "when"), we use the simple present ("I reach"), not "will reach".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "He will be" and "waiting for me when" are correct (future continuous).

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: I/you/we/they + base verb (I reach, they go); he/she/it + verb-s (he reaches). Also, in time clauses after "when/until/before", use the simple present for future meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

All in the same boat
option_1: When everyone is dealing with the same situation
option_2: When everyone has to start all over again
option_3: When a task can be accomplished together
option_4: When everybody is travelling in the same vehicle
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. When everyone is dealing with the same situation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(all) in the same boat" means being in the same difficult or unfortunate situation as others. (एक ही (कठिन) परिस्थिति में होना)

◦ Example: When the company cut everyone's pay, we were all in the same boat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 takes the idiom literally (a vehicle/boat); Options 2 and 3 do not capture the "shared difficult situation" sense.

NOTE

• The idiom stresses a shared (usually difficult) predicament. Similar expressions: "in the same position", "facing the same problem".

question:
Select the most appropriate verb form to fill in the blank in the given sentence.

She __________ her keys on the kitchen counter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. laid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "lay" (to put/place something down) is transitive and takes an object ("her keys"). Its simple past is "laid". The sentence describes a completed action (placing the keys), so "laid" is correct.

◦ Correct: She laid her keys on the kitchen counter.

• Forms: lay – laid – laid (transitive, needs an object).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lays" (present) is possible but "laid" fits a completed action better; more importantly, options 3 "lying" and 4 "lain" belong to the intransitive verb "lie".

• Option 3 "lying" and Option 4 "lain" are forms of "lie" (to recline), which is intransitive and takes no object.

NOTE

• Lay (transitive, needs object): lay–laid–laid → "lay the keys down". Lie (intransitive, no object): lie–lay–lain → "lie on the bed". The lay/lie distinction is a frequent SSC trap.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The new/ smartphone is/ absolutely best than/ the latest model.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. absolutely best than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree, not the superlative. So "best than" is wrong; it should be "better than".

◦ Correct: The new smartphone is absolutely better than the latest model.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The new", "smartphone is" and "the latest model" are all correct.

NOTE

• Degrees of "good": good – better (with "than") – best (with "the"). Use the comparative "better" with "than"; use the superlative "best" with "the".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The brave and courageous soldiers / of our motherland / fell into the enemy / and won the battle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. fell into the enemy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "fall upon/on" (to attack), not "fall into". So it should be "fell upon/on the enemy".

◦ Correct: The brave and courageous soldiers of our motherland fell upon the enemy and won the battle.

• "Fall into" means to enter a state/condition or land inside something, which does not fit "attacking the enemy".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The brave and courageous soldiers", "of our motherland" and "and won the battle" are all correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "fall": fall upon/on (attack), fall into (enter a state — fall into a habit/trap), fall out (quarrel), fall through (fail), fall back on (rely on).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Whenever addressed, she comes _____ and performs her _____ in a great way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. forth, role.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forth" means forward/onward ("comes forth" = comes forward), and "role" means a part/function one performs. So "she comes forth and performs her role in a great way". (आगे आना; भूमिका)

◦ Correct: Whenever addressed, she comes forth and performs her role in a great way.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Fourth" (4th, an ordinal number) and "roll" (to turn over / a list) are homophones but wrong in this context.

NOTE

• Confusable pairs: forth (forward) / fourth (4th); role (a part/function) / roll (to turn / a list / a bread roll).

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.

Self-esteem is an important aspekt of one's self.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. aspect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "aspect", meaning a particular part or feature of something. (पहलू / पक्ष)

◦ Example: We must consider every aspect of the problem.

• Spelling key: A + SPECT — ends in "-spect" (from Latin "spectare", to look; as in inspect, respect, prospect).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "aspet", 2 "aspikt" and 4 "aaspet" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Words with "-spect" (to look): aspect, respect, inspect, prospect, suspect, spectator, spectacle.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The keys were lies on the table.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. lying on the table.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "were" (past continuous), we need the present participle (-ing form). The intransitive verb "lie" (to be positioned/rest) gives "lying". So "The keys were lying on the table."

◦ Correct: The keys were lying on the table.

• "were lies" is grammatically wrong; "were + V-ing" is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "lay" (past of lie) and Option 4 "lie" (base form) cannot follow "were".

NOTE

• "Lie" (to rest/be positioned): lie–lay–lain, present participle "lying". "The book is lying on the table" (not "laying"). Do not confuse with "lay" (to put something down).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Manish has being applying / for colleges / ever since he passed / his entrance test in March.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. manish has being applying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct form of the present perfect continuous tense is "has been + V-ing", not "has being". So "has being applying" should be "has been applying".

◦ Correct: Manish has been applying for colleges ever since he passed his entrance test in March.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "for colleges", "ever since he passed" and "his entrance test in March" are all correct.

NOTE

• Present perfect continuous = has/have been + V-ing (has been applying). "Been" (past participle of "be") is used here, NOT "being". Use with "since/for/ever since" for actions continuing up to now.

question:
Based on the situation in the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.

There are several people who find themselves a dominating person in a group
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cock of the walk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "cock of the walk" refers to a person who dominates others within a group; someone who behaves as if they are the most important. (समूह में दबदबा रखने वाला व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: Ever since his promotion, he has been the cock of the walk in the office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a bone of contention" (a subject of dispute), Option 2 "a man of his words" (one who keeps promises) and Option 4 "a white elephant" (a costly but useless possession) do not fit.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from the image of a rooster (cock) that dominates the farmyard. It means a domineering, self-important person in a group.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The pencil has a tip made of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. lead.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The writing core of a pencil is commonly (though loosely) called "lead" (it is actually graphite). So "The pencil has a tip made of lead." (सीसा / पेंसिल की लीड)

◦ Example: The pencil's lead broke while she was writing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "led" (past tense of "lead" — to guide) is a homophone but wrong here.

• Option 2 "lewd" (obscene) and Option 4 "steal" (to take unlawfully — a homophone of "steel") are unrelated.

NOTE

• Note the homophones/confusables: lead (the metal/pencil core — noun) vs lead (to guide — verb, past "led"); steal (to rob) vs steel (the metal).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

Jared deliberately set fire to a property and got arrested by the police.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Arson.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arson" is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property. It exactly matches "deliberately set fire to a property". (आगजनी / अग्निदाह — एक अपराध)

◦ Example: The factory fire was found to be a case of arson.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Dystrophy" (a disorder involving the wasting of tissues), Option 3 "Insomnia" (inability to sleep) and Option 4 "Dementia" (loss of mental ability) are medical conditions, not crimes.

NOTE

• A person who commits arson is an "arsonist". Related crime-related one-word substitutes: burglary (breaking in to steal), theft/larceny, homicide (killing).

question:
Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank.

The underground railway network, 'The Tube' in London is said to be __________ transport in London.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the most expensive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing the Tube as the costliest of all transport in London requires the superlative degree with the definite article "the" — "the most expensive transport in London".

◦ Correct: ... 'The Tube' in London is said to be the most expensive transport in London.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "expensive" (positive) and Option 3 "the expensive" lack the superlative sense.

• Option 4 "more expensive" is the comparative (used with "than").

NOTE

• Long adjectives form the superlative with "the most" (the most expensive, the most beautiful) and the comparative with "more ... than". The phrase "in London" (a whole group) signals the superlative.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ___1___ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ___2___ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any ___3___ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ___4___ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ___5___ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. would.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Would" is used to describe a repeated/habitual action in the past. Whenever his car stopped, voices "would shout out his name" — a habitual past event. (भूतकालीन आदत)

◦ Correct: Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices would shout out his name.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "can" (present ability), Option 2 "should" (advice/obligation) and Option 4 "could" (past ability/possibility) do not convey the repeated past action as well as "would".

NOTE

• "Would" (and "used to") express past habits/repeated actions: "Every summer, we would visit our grandparents." Here the habitual shouting whenever the car stopped requires "would".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ___1___ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ___2___ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any ___3___ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ___4___ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ___5___ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "as" means "when / while" — it introduces a clause of time. "Policemen ... waved and smiled as he passed" = while/when he passed. (जब / जैसे ही)

◦ Correct: Policemen, agricultural labourers ... and priests waved and smiled as he passed ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "nor" (used with "neither"), Option 2 "so" (therefore) and Option 4 "thus" (in this way) do not fit as a time connector here.

NOTE

• "As" has several meanings: (1) when/while (time — as he passed), (2) because (reason — as it was late), (3) in the way that (manner). Here it means "when/while".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ___1___ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ___2___ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any ___3___ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ___4___ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ___5___ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. form.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Form" here means a type or kind. "Any form of Governmental red tape" = any type/kind of bureaucratic delay. (रूप / प्रकार)

◦ Correct: ... his ... fearlessness when dealing with any form of Governmental red tape.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "forum" (a place/meeting for discussion), Option 3 "from" (a preposition) and Option 4 "farm" (agricultural land) do not fit "any ___ of".

NOTE

• "Red tape" is an idiom meaning excessive official rules/bureaucracy that cause delay. "Any form of red tape" = any kind of bureaucratic hurdle.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ___1___ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ___2___ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any ___3___ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ___4___ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ___5___ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. confiscated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Confiscated" means officially seized/taken away (by an authority). The cases had been confiscated by the Customs on the ground that they were merchandise. (जब्त किया गया)

◦ Correct: ... two of our cases ... had been confiscated by the Customs ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "contributed" (donated), Option 2 "concealed" (hidden) and Option 4 "collected" (gathered) do not fit the sense of the Customs officially seizing goods.

NOTE

• "Confiscate" = to seize (property) with authority. Customs authorities confiscate goods that violate rules. Synonyms: seize, impound, appropriate.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ___1___ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ___2___ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any ___3___ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ___4___ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ___5___ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "About" here means "concerning / regarding". Mother told Spiro about our cases in the Customs (i.e., informed him regarding the cases) and asked for his advice. (के बारे में)

◦ Correct: ... Mother told Spiro about our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "within" (inside), Option 3 "from" and Option 4 "behind" do not fit the sense of telling someone regarding a matter.

NOTE

• "Tell someone about something" = to inform someone regarding a matter. Here Mother informed Spiro about the confiscated cases to seek his advice.

question: Who among the following was the founder of Indian Association in Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surendra Nath Banerjee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Indian Association" (Indian National Association) was founded in 1876 in Calcutta (Bengal) by Surendra Nath Banerjee (along with Ananda Mohan Bose). It was one of the earliest political organisations in India. (भारतीय संघ — सुरेंद्रनाथ बनर्जी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Surendra Nath Banerjee was a moderate nationalist leader, often called "Rashtraguru" and the "Indian Burke".

• The Indian Association aimed to create a strong public opinion and unite Indians on political questions; it merged with the Indian National Congress later.

NOTE

• The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume. Early moderate leaders included Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Surendra Nath Banerjee.

question: Usain Bolt shared the journey of his life in which of the following autobiographies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Faster Than Lightning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Faster Than Lightning" is the autobiography of the legendary Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt, the fastest man in the world. (उसेन बोल्ट की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Usain Bolt holds the world records in the 100 m (9.58 s) and 200 m sprints and has won 8 Olympic gold medals.

• He is nicknamed "Lightning Bolt" for his incredible speed.

NOTE

• Sports autobiographies: Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Open (Andre Agassi), The Race of My Life (Milkha Singh), Unbreakable (Mary Kom).

question: According to Newland's Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first element. Which of the following elements has properties similar to those of N?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Newland's Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to the first (like the eighth note in a musical octave). Starting from Nitrogen (N), the eighth element is Phosphorus (P) — both belong to the same group (Group 15) and have similar properties. (न्यूलैंड्स का अष्टक नियम — N और P)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• John Newlands (1866) arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass and found this repeating pattern of properties every eighth element.

• The law worked only for lighter elements (up to calcium) and failed for heavier ones.

NOTE

• Development of the periodic table: Dobereiner's Triads → Newland's Law of Octaves → Mendeleev's Periodic Table (based on atomic mass) → Modern Periodic Table (Moseley, based on atomic number).

question: __________ is mainly celebrated by Maharashtrians as New Year's Day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gudi Padwa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gudi Padwa" is celebrated mainly by Maharashtrians as their New Year's Day. It marks the beginning of the traditional (Chaitra) new year and the spring season. (गुड़ी पड़वा — महाराष्ट्र का नववर्ष)

• A "Gudi" (a decorated pole with a bright cloth and a garland) is raised outside homes on this day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The same New Year (around March–April) is celebrated as Ugadi in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and Cheti Chand by the Sindhi community.

• Pongal (Tamil Nadu) and Bihu (Assam) are harvest festivals.

NOTE

• Regional New Year festivals: Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Ugadi (AP/Telangana/Karnataka), Baisakhi (Punjab), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Bihu/Rongali (Assam), Navroz (Parsi).

question: Who among the following was sent by Akbar to lead the Mughal army in the Battle of Haldighati which was fought in 1576?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Man Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Battle of Haldighati (1576), the Mughal army was led by Raja Man Singh (of Amber), who was sent by Emperor Akbar. The battle was fought against Maharana Pratap of Mewar. (हल्दीघाटी युद्ध, 1576 — राजा मानसिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Battle of Haldighati was fought near Haldighati (Rajasthan); despite fierce resistance, Maharana Pratap could not be captured and continued his struggle against the Mughals.

• Maharana Pratap's loyal horse "Chetak" is legendary; Raja Man Singh was one of Akbar's Navaratnas.

NOTE

• Maharana Pratap is remembered as a symbol of valour and resistance against Mughal expansion. He later recovered much of Mewar (except Chittor).

question: Which Fundamental Right guarantees protection of interests of the minorities in the matter of their language, script or culture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cultural and Educational Rights.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Cultural and Educational Rights" (Articles 29 and 30) guarantee the protection of the interests of minorities in the matter of their language, script and culture, and their right to establish and administer educational institutions. (सांस्कृतिक एवं शैक्षिक अधिकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 29 — protects the interests of minorities (any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture).

• Article 30 — gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights (Part III): Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

question: Which state finished second in the first edition of the Khelo India Para Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the first edition of the Khelo India Para Games (held in December 2023 at New Delhi), Haryana finished first and Uttar Pradesh finished second in the medal tally. (खेलो इंडिया पैरा गेम्स — उत्तर प्रदेश दूसरे स्थान पर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Khelo India Para Games are a national multi-sport event for para-athletes (differently-abled players), part of the wider Khelo India programme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

• The first edition included sports like para-athletics, para-badminton, para-table tennis, para-powerlifting and shooting.

NOTE

• The Khelo India programme also includes the Khelo India Youth Games, University Games and Winter Games, aimed at promoting sports at the grassroots level.

question: Select the odd one from the following saltwater lakes on the basis of their formation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sambhar lake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sambhar Lake" is the odd one out because it is an inland (continental) saltwater lake in Rajasthan, formed in an arid region, whereas Pulicat, Kolleru and Chilika are coastal lakes/lagoons (formed along the coast). (साम्भर झील — अंतर्देशीय खारी झील)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan) is India's largest inland saltwater lake and a major source of salt production.

• Chilika (Odisha) is the largest coastal lagoon; Pulicat (AP/TN) is the second-largest; Kolleru (AP) is a large freshwater/coastal lake.

NOTE

• Coastal lagoons are formed when a sandbar/spit separates a part of the sea; inland saltwater lakes form in arid basins where water evaporates leaving salts behind.

question: If the tax rate increases with the taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is progressive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "progressive tax" is one in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount (base/income) increases — i.e., the rich pay a higher percentage than the poor. (प्रगामी/प्रगतिशील कर)

◦ Example: India's income tax is progressive (higher income slabs are taxed at higher rates).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Regressive tax — the tax rate decreases as income increases (falls more heavily on the poor).

• Proportional tax — the tax rate stays the same regardless of income (a flat rate).

• Digressive tax — progressive up to a limit, then a flat/uniform rate beyond it.

NOTE

• Taxes are of two types: Direct taxes (income tax, corporate tax — borne by the person taxed) and Indirect taxes (GST, customs duty — passed on to consumers). Direct taxes are usually progressive.

question: As of February 2024, who among the following is the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harivansh Narayan Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of February 2024, Harivansh Narayan Singh was the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. (राज्यसभा के उपसभापति — हरिवंश नारायण सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is elected from among the members of the House and presides over its proceedings in the absence of the Chairman.

• The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President of India (ex-officio, under Article 89).

NOTE

• In the Lok Sabha, the presiding officers are the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, both elected from among the members.

question: In October 2023, Indrasena Reddy Nallu has been appointed the Governor of which of the following states in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2023, Indrasena Reddy Nallu was appointed the Governor of Tripura. (त्रिपुरा के राज्यपाल — इंद्रसेन रेड्डी नल्लू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President under Article 155, and holds office during the President's pleasure (Article 156).

• Tripura is a state in North-East India; its capital is Agartala.

NOTE

• A Governor must be a citizen of India and at least 35 years of age. The same person can be appointed as Governor of two or more states.

question: Vinod Mankara's documentary 'Mohiniyattathinte Amma' is based on which of the following world renowned Mohiniyattam dancers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinod Mankara's documentary "Mohiniyattathinte Amma" (The Mother of Mohiniyattam) is based on the legendary Mohiniyattam dancer Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, who is regarded as the "Mother of Mohiniyattam". (कलामंडलम कल्याणीकुट्टी अम्मा — मोहिनीअट्टम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma played a key role in the revival and systematisation of Mohiniyattam.

• Mohiniyattam is a graceful, feminine classical dance form of Kerala (the "dance of the enchantress/Mohini").

NOTE

• The classical dances of Kerala are Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Mohiniyattam is characterised by gentle, swaying movements and white-and-gold costumes.

question: Identify the INCORRECT pair (State and Iron-ore producing region) from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh - Ratnagiri (this pair is INCORRECT).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pair "Madhya Pradesh – Ratnagiri" is incorrect because Ratnagiri is an iron-ore producing district of MAHARASHTRA (in the Konkan region), not Madhya Pradesh. (रत्नागिरी — महाराष्ट्र, मध्य प्रदेश नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The correctly matched pairs:

◦ Odisha – Badampahar (Mayurbhanj district).

◦ Karnataka – Kudremukh (famous iron-ore mines).

◦ Chhattisgarh – Bailadila (high-grade hematite, exported to Japan).

NOTE

• Major iron-ore belts of India: Odisha–Jharkhand belt, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt (Chhattisgarh-Maharashtra), Bellary-Chitradurga belt (Karnataka), and Maharashtra-Goa belt.

question: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was constructed in around 1197 AD by the sultan of which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mamluk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque" (in the Qutub complex, Delhi) was constructed around 1197 AD by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. (कुव्वत-उल-इस्लाम मस्जिद — मामलूक/गुलाम वंश)

• It is regarded as one of the earliest mosques built in India after the establishment of the Sultanate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Qutb-ud-din Aibak also began the construction of the Qutub Minar, which was later completed by Iltutmish.

• The Mamluk/Slave dynasty (1206–1290) was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

NOTE

• The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate: Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khalji (1290), Tughlaq (1320), Sayyid (1414) and Lodi (1451).

question: The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is plasmodesmata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plasmodesmata" (singular: plasmodesma) are the microscopic channels that pass through the cell walls of adjacent plant cells (and some algae), connecting them and allowing the transport of substances and communication between the cells. (प्लाज्मोडेस्माटा — पादप कोशिकाओं के बीच सूक्ष्म चैनल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring plant cells, forming a continuous network called the symplast.

• Ribosomes make proteins; lysosomes digest waste; desmosomes are cell junctions in animal cells.

NOTE

• Plant cells have a rigid cell wall (made of cellulose); plasmodesmata are the "bridges" that allow communication across these walls, similar to gap junctions in animal cells.

question:
Select the INCORRECT statement.

A) Functional segments of DNA are called genes.  B) The chromatin material gets organised into rod-shaped chromosomes only when the cell is about to divide.  C) Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates.  D) DNA molecules contain the information necessary for constructing and organising cells.
option_1: Functional segments of DNA are called genes.
option_2: The chromatin material gets organised into rod-shaped chromosomes only when the cell is about to divide.
option_3: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates.
option_4: DNA molecules contain the information necessary for constructing and organising cells.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates (this statement is INCORRECT).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement C is incorrect: chromosomes are composed of DNA and PROTEINS (histones), NOT carbohydrates. (गुणसूत्र — डीएनए एवं प्रोटीन से बने, कार्बोहाइड्रेट से नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other statements are correct:

◦ A — Functional segments of DNA that code for traits are called genes.

◦ B — Chromatin condenses into rod-shaped chromosomes only during cell division.

◦ D — DNA carries the genetic information for building and organising cells.

NOTE

• A chromosome = DNA + proteins (histones). Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). The DNA–protein complex is called chromatin, which condenses into visible chromosomes during cell division.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which states of India have population density more than 1000 persons per sq. km?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar and West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, among the given options, Bihar (1,106 persons/sq. km) and West Bengal (1,028 persons/sq. km) are the states with a population density of more than 1,000 persons per sq. km. (बिहार एवं पश्चिम बंगाल — 1000+ जनसंख्या घनत्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bihar had the highest population density among the states (1,106) as per Census 2011.

• Among Union Territories, Delhi has the highest density; the National Capital Territory of Delhi is extremely densely populated.

NOTE

• Population density = total population ÷ total area (persons per sq. km). India's overall density in 2011 was about 382 persons/sq. km. Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density among states.

question: Krishnarao Shankar Pandit belonged to which of the following music gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gwalior gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Krishnarao Shankar Pandit was a distinguished Hindustani classical vocalist who belonged to the Gwalior gharana, the oldest gharana of Hindustani khayal music. (ग्वालियर घराना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Gwalior gharana is considered the fountainhead of the khayal style; many other gharanas developed from it.

• Krishnarao Shankar Pandit was awarded the Padma Bhushan; he was known for his mastery of layakari (rhythmic play).

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Mewati and Rampur-Sahaswan.

question: Which executive system is present in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parliamentary System.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has a "Parliamentary System" of executive, adopted from the British (Westminster) model. In this system, the executive is responsible to the legislature (Parliament). (संसदीय शासन प्रणाली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Key features of the parliamentary system:

◦ A nominal executive (President) and a real executive (Prime Minister and Council of Ministers).

◦ Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha (Article 75).

◦ Majority-party rule and the possibility of dissolution of the Lower House.

• The Presidential System (as in the USA) has a strict separation of powers, with the President as both Head of State and Head of Government.

NOTE

• The parliamentary system operates at both the Union (President–PM) and State (Governor–CM) levels in India.

question: Which of the following is the National waterway no. 4 in India?
option_1: Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers and East Coast Canal
option_2: The Brahmaputra river between Sadiya and Dhubri
option_3: Godavari and Krishna rivers along with Kakinada Puducherry
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari and Krishna rivers along with Kakinada Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Waterway No. 4 (NW-4) comprises the Godavari and Krishna rivers along with the Kakinada–Puducherry canal system (and related canals). (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग-4 — गोदावरी-कृष्णा एवं काकीनाडा-पुडुचेरी नहर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Major National Waterways:

◦ NW-1: Ganga (Prayagraj/Allahabad – Haldia).

◦ NW-2: Brahmaputra (Sadiya – Dhubri).

◦ NW-3: West Coast Canal (Kerala).

◦ NW-4: Godavari–Krishna + Kakinada–Puducherry canals.

◦ NW-5: Mahanadi–Brahmani + East Coast Canal.

NOTE

• National Waterways are declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016, and managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) for cheap, eco-friendly water transport.

question: The Irani Cup is a first-class cricket competition played between the winner of the Ranji Trophy and which other team?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rest of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Irani Cup" (Irani Trophy) is a first-class cricket competition played between the winner of the Ranji Trophy and a "Rest of India" team. (ईरानी कप — रणजी विजेता बनाम शेष भारत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Irani Cup was started in the 1959–60 season to mark the 25th anniversary of the Ranji Trophy; it is named after Z. R. Irani, a former BCCI official.

• The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket tournament (started 1934), named after Ranjitsinhji.

NOTE

• Major domestic cricket tournaments in India: Ranji Trophy (first-class), Irani Cup, Duleep Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy (List A/one-day) and the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20).

question: A 5% decrease in poverty by 2007 was one of main objectives of the __________ plan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tenth Year Plan (2002-2007).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A 5% reduction in the poverty ratio by 2007 was one of the main objectives/monitorable targets of the Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007). (दसवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Tenth Plan aimed at a growth rate of 8% and set several "monitorable targets", including reducing poverty, providing gainful employment, and improving literacy and health indicators.

• Five-Year Plans in India were formulated by the Planning Commission (now replaced by NITI Aayog since 2015).

NOTE

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused on agriculture (Harrod–Domar model); the planning era ended after the Twelfth Plan (2012–17).

question: Who among the following launched the Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annie Besant launched her "Home Rule League" in September 1916 at Madras (Chennai). The movement demanded self-government (Home Rule) for India within the British Empire. (होम रूल लीग — एनी बेसेंट, 1916)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak had earlier launched his Home Rule League in April 1916 at Belgaum (Poona) with the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it".

• Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1917, Calcutta session).

NOTE

• The two Home Rule Leagues (Tilak's and Besant's) worked in different regions to create a strong demand for self-rule, especially during the First World War.

question: Tax, known as bhaga, was levied on which of the following during Mahajanapada period of Ancient India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tax on cultivators.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the Mahajanapada period of ancient India, "Bhaga" was the tax levied on cultivators (farmers) — it was a share of the agricultural produce (usually one-sixth) paid to the king. (भाग — किसानों पर लगने वाला कर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Bhaga" literally means "a share"; the king's share of the produce was commonly one-sixth, so the king was called "Shadbhagin" (the receiver of one-sixth).

• The Mahajanapadas (c. 6th century BCE) were 16 large kingdoms/republics; Magadha eventually became the most powerful.

NOTE

• Other ancient taxes: Bali (a tribute/tax), Shulka (customs/toll), Kara (a periodic tax). Land revenue (from cultivators) was the main source of state income.

question: In 2022, Arjun Singh Dhurve was honoured with the Padma Shri Award for his contribution in which of the following Indian folk-dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2022, Arjun Singh Dhurve was honoured with the Padma Shri for his contribution to the "Baiga" tribal folk dance of the Baiga tribe (found mainly in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh). (बैगा नृत्य — अर्जुन सिंह धुर्वे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Baiga are a tribal community known for their rich culture, and their folk dances are performed during festivals and special occasions.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, given for distinguished contribution in various fields, including art and culture.

NOTE

• Folk/tribal dances for SSC: Baiga (MP/Chhattisgarh), Laho (Meghalaya), Bihu (Assam), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/Bengal), Karma (tribal Central India).
